name: Tate McRae
description:
'''Tate Rosner McRae''' (born July 1, 2003) is a Canadian singer, songwriter, and dancer. McRae began her career as a dancer, appearing as a contestant on the American reality television series ''[[So You Think You Can Dance (American TV series)|So You Think You Can Dance]]'' in 2016. After signing with [[RCA Records]], she released the [[extended play]]s (EPs) ''[[All the Things I Never Said (Tate McRae EP)|All the Things I Never Said]]'' (2020) and ''[[Too Young to Be Sad]]'' (2021); the latter became the most streamed female EP of 2021 on [[Spotify]], while its single "[[You Broke Me First]]" marked her first US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] entry. She released her debut studio album, ''[[I Used to Think I Could Fly]]'', the following year. 

McRae's second studio album, ''[[Think Later]]'' (2023), explored a more [[pop music|pop]]-oriented sound and was led by the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]] number-one single "[[Greedy (Tate McRae song)|Greedy]]". In 2025, she topped the US [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]  with her third studio album, ''[[So Close to What]]'',  and scored her first US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] number-one single with the duet "[[What I Want (Morgan Wallen song)|What I Want]]". She also earned a [[Grammy Award for Best Dance Pop Recording|Grammy Award]] nomination for the [[F1 the Album|soundtrack]] single "[[Just Keep Watching]]".
